newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa futures close mixed, nearbys weak.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa futures close mixed, nearbys weak.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures ended mixed on Wednesday, with nearby months weakest. traders said.

May closed down nine stg at 966 stg per tonne and July shed four to 997. Total volume stood at 8,255 contracts, with July grabbing 3,933 lots. May came in second with 2,195 contracts. All other months traded fewer than 1,000 lots.
Cocoa had opened slightly higher, trying to recover some of Tuesday afternoon's steep losses. But the upside was limited and prices slipped again.
July broke support at 1,000 and fell a stg below next support at 990 to reach the lowest level since April 9.
Next key support rests at 980, the April 9 low.

Some traders speculated the latest sell-off surfaced when it appeared that no play was being made in May cocoa. May's first notice day is on Thursday, and the open interest in May had looked like someone was trying to hold cocoa.
But May open interest fell sharply on Tuesday to allay those fears. Uncovered May positions shed 4,122 contracts to 2,209, and open positions lost 5,315 to 3,810.
Traders said the change in the market's structure in the latest drop reflected that relief. July's premium over December narrowed sharply to two stg from about 21 just a week ago.
September was at a 12-stg premium to December.
Once most speculative and fund liquidation dried up on Tuesday, traders said some funds entered as fresh sellers.
But they said funds in New York still seemed to be net long cocoa, which could keep the market under pressure.

Broker GNI also slashed its world cocoa deficit forecast in 1996/97 to 33,000 tonnes from 180,000 due to an increase in expectations for the Ivorian crop. In its daily commentary, it said "we would not even rule out a marginal supply surplus if the mid-crop comes in as large as some traders are predicting."

German cocoa consumers were also seen placing some orders for second-half 1997 and first-quarter 1998 beans against sharply lower futures, but sterling's recent strength has dampened interest, physical traders said.
But Hamburg traders said they did not expect cocoa prices to spin into freefall because West African mid-crop progress seemed slow and shipments were still delayed.
In Germany, cocoa butter demand was flat though the butter ratio over futures has slipped 15 points over the last month.
Ivory Coast semi-finished cocoa product and powder exports fell to 6,530 tonnes in March from February's 8,830 tonnes, but cocoa bean exports jumped to 171,104 tonnes versus February's 148,827.
French January cocoa bean imports also rose year on year.
In the near-term, most traders expected more downside for cocoa. They said July's fair value was probably closer to about 960.

Technically, July closed above support at 990 but remained vulnerable to more losses and a test of 980. But volume is expected to thin out this week before a three-day holiday weekend in the UK. Markets here are closed on Monday for a bank holiday.
No options traded, according to LIFFE.
--Medora Lee, London newsroom +44 171 542 8072
